reconcile.note: John Gill reads God's question in Genesis 3:9 as a rhetorical summons meant to draw out confession, not evidence that he lacked knowledge of Adam's location.

discrepancy.note: Wellhausen treats the Yahwist's God as anthropomorphic and non-omniscient, a general trait of which this garden search is one instance.

quotes.text: In the evening when it grows cool He goes to walk in the garden, and when there discovers by chance the transgression which has taken place, and holds an investigation in which He makes not the least use of His omniscience.
quotes.attr: Julius Wellhausen (d. 1918), Prolegomena to the History of Israel (1885), on the anthropomorphic, non-omniscient God of the Yahwist's garden narrative.

sides.verseText: Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, \"Where are you?\"

sides.snippet: because if our heart condemns us, God is greater than our heart, and knows all things.
